spans.s:
Yati is the name of an ancient clan which is connected with the Bhṛgus in two passages of the Rigveda, where the Yatis certainly seem to be real persons. In another hymn, however, they already appear as almost mythical. In the yajurveda Saṃhitās, and elsewhere, the Yatis are a race whom indra, in an evil moment, gave over to the hyænas (sālāvṛka): exactly what is referred to is uncertain. yati is mentioned with bhṛgu in a verse of the sāmaveda.

Yātu-dhāna in the Rigveda and later denotes a ‘sorcerer,’ ‘wizard,’ or ‘magician.’ The sense of the Rigveda is clearly unfavourable to sorcery. The feminine, Yātudhānī, is also found in the Rigveda and later.
